chief_complaint: Management of hypertension and associated metabolic risk factors (obesity, prediabetes) with concern for low blood pressure and overall cardiovascular health.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a long-standing history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2005, currently treated with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Recent vital signs show a low-normal blood pressure of 96/57 mmHg, raising concern for possible overtreatment. She has obesity (BMI ≥30) documented since 2002 and prediabetes with an A1c of 6.2% noted in 2021. Anemia was also identified in 2021, etiology unknown. Chronic sinusitis has been present since 2020, with prior episodes of acute bacterial and viral sinusitis. She reports ongoing psychosocial stressors including intimate partner abuse, limited social contact, and low educational attainment, all of which may impact adherence and lifestyle modification. She is employed full‑time and uses a levonorgestrel intrauterine system for contraception. No recent emergency or inpatient encounters have occurred; most visits are outpatient wellness appointments.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple medication reviews (2020‑2022), prior stress, acute bacterial and viral sinusitis episodes (2019‑2020), unhealthy alcohol use resolved in 2022, prior acute infective cystitis (2019), and a period of not being in the labor force (2021). The patient also has a history of miscarriage in 2002.
social_determinants: Intimate partner abuse, limited social contact, low educational attainment (primary school only), full‑time employment, and a history of unhealthy alcohol use (resolved). These factors likely affect health literacy, medication adherence, and ability to engage in lifestyle interventions.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: hypertension (treated), obesity, prediabetes (A1c 6.2%), likely dyslipidemia (lipid panel missing). Renal risk: hypertension and thiazide use; eGFR not available. Hematologic risk: anemia of unknown etiology. ENT risk: chronic sinusitis with prior acute infections. Psychosocial risk: intimate partner violence, limited social support, low education. Current vitals show low-normal BP (96/57) suggesting possible overtreatment. Charlson comorbidity index is 1; clinical complexity is moderate.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with a cluster of metabolic risk factors (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes) and anemia, compounded by chronic sinusitis and significant psychosocial stressors including intimate partner violence and limited social support.
